custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active tracked part, part A, for this test with 2 in its bin and a Core Charge of $25.00, so it has a core.
  • Use a computer that can open the exported file in a spreadsheet program.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C573676-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C573676-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • Theme: click your avatar (the AS circle) at the top right; Light and Dark are at the bottom of its menu.
  • Export is in the Inventory list's three-dot actions menu (with Cycle count and Deactivate parts); it downloads a file.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • No row is listed for the core: the list shows its usual empty result.

Step 2:

  • Exactly one row is listed, part A, with $25.00 in its Core column; there is no second row for its core.

Step 3:

  • The menu opens.

Step 4:

  • A file downloads.

Step 5:

  • The file holds one part row, part A; there is no row for its core.

Step 6:

  • The menu opens.

Step 7:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 8:

  • The bar reads 1 selected: the header checkbox ticked part A only, because its core has no row that could be ticked.

Step 9:

  • Bulk mode ends and nothing was deactivated.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part), story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List), story SV-10815 (Story 2, Deactivate Parts in Bulk)

  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history are recorded on the core's own Part History page, which has no link on screen in this release. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • S1-R9b: “The export includes every part on that tab that matches the current search, filters and Supply filter, including parts not yet scrolled into view. With nothing matching, the message "Empty export" shows and no file is made.”
  • S2-R6: “The checkbox in the header ticks or clears every row loaded in the list. The list loads 30 parts at a time as the user scrolls, so it ticks only the rows loaded so far. The count in the bar shows exactly how many parts will change.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.
